engineSelect.heading: Choose how your chart is calculated
engineSelect.lead: Astrologers differ a little on where the zodiac begins and how the twelve houses are drawn. Not sure? Leave it on Lahiri, the one most Indian astrologers use.
engineSelect.guidanceStep2: 2. Pick the house style from its dropdown
engineSelect.guidanceStep3: 3. Generate the chart with that method
engineSelect.summaryImpactText: The tradition sets where each sign begins, so a planet can land a degree or two either side of a boundary. The style changes where the house lines fall.

lahiri.label: Lahiri
lahiri.description: The standard across India. If you are not sure, use this one.
lahiri.method: Lahiri anchors the sidereal zodiac to the traditional Chitra/Spica reference used in mainstream Indian panchang and ephemeris work.
lahiri.summary: The mainstream Vedic choice, and the safest general-purpose option.

raman.label: Raman
raman.description: A small shift away from Lahiri, taught in B. V. Raman's school.
raman.method: Raman uses a separate precession offset from Lahiri, so planets and cusps can shift subtly near sign or house boundaries.
raman.summary: An alternative Vedic reading, for comparing against Lahiri.

krishnamurti.label: Krishnamurti
krishnamurti.description: The KP system, used for pinning down timing and specific events.
krishnamurti.method: KP combines its own ayanamsha with house cusps and sub-lord analysis, making it popular for event-focused readings.
krishnamurti.summary: Built for detailed prediction and event timing.

fagan_bradley.label: Fagan-Bradley
fagan_bradley.description: The Western sidereal standard, used for side-by-side comparisons.
fagan_bradley.method: Fagan-Bradley follows the Swiss Ephemeris reference value of 24.042044444 degrees at JD 2433282.42346.
fagan_bradley.summary: The Western sidereal reference, for comparative work.

pushyapaksha.label: Pushyapaksha
pushyapaksha.description: Anchored to the star Pushya instead of to a calculated value.
pushyapaksha.method: Pushyapaksha follows the True Pushya rule: Asellus Australis / delta Cancri is set to 16 degrees Cancer.
pushyapaksha.summary: A star-anchored reference, fixed to Pushya.

yukteshwar.label: Yukteshwar
yukteshwar.description: Follows the lineage of Sri Yukteshwar.
yukteshwar.method: Yukteshwar follows the Swiss Ephemeris reference value 360 - 338.917778 degrees at J1900.0.
yukteshwar.summary: An alternative sidereal reading in Sri Yukteshwar's lineage.

whole_sign.label: Classic Whole Sign
whole_sign.description: One whole sign per house, counted from your rising sign. The usual Vedic choice.

equal.label: Equal Houses
equal.description: Twelve houses of exactly 30 degrees, measured from your rising degree.

placidus.label: Placidus
placidus.description: House sizes vary with the time of day. Standard in Western astrology and in KP work.

koch.label: Koch
koch.description: Like Placidus, but worked out from your birthplace.

campanus.label: Campanus
campanus.description: Houses divided up by direction in the sky rather than by time.

regiomontanus.label: Regiomontanus
regiomontanus.description: A medieval system, divided along the celestial equator.

navamsa.heading: Navamsa (D9)
navamsa.introText: The Navamsa (D9) is the most important divisional chart in Vedic astrology. It reveals the soul's deeper purpose, the nature of marriage and partnerships, and the strength of planetary placements at a dharmic level. When a planet occupies the same sign in both the Rashi and Navamsa charts, it achieves Vargottama status — a mark of exceptional strength.

facts.aries1: The first sign · ruled by Mars, it carries the spark of new beginnings and the courage to step into the unknown.
facts.aries2: In Vedic lore the Sun is exalted in Mesha · the spring equinox once anchored the year's true beginning here.
facts.taurus1: Venus's earthy domain · patient, sensual, and steadfast as the bull that guards the field.
facts.taurus2: The Pleiades sit on Taurus' shoulder · Vedic seers call these seven sisters Krittika, the flame nymphs.
facts.gemini1: Castor is not one star but six · a sextuple system bound by gravity, masquerading as a single point of light.
facts.gemini2: Mercury's airy twins · the messenger sign of curiosity, language, and the threshold between worlds.
facts.cancer1: The Moon's own house · Vedic tradition names it Karka, the keeper of memory, lineage, and the inner tide.
facts.cancer2: At its heart lies the Beehive Cluster, M44 · a swarm of nearly a thousand stars Galileo first resolved in 1609.
facts.leo1: Regulus, the Little King, sits almost exactly on the ecliptic · the Sun crosses it directly each August.
facts.leo2: In Vedic tradition Simha is the Sun's own house · royalty, gold, and the spine all answer to its rulership.
facts.virgo1: The second-largest constellation in the sky · Virgo sprawls across 1,294 square degrees of celestial real estate.
facts.virgo2: Mercury is exalted here · in Vedic lore Kanya holds the discernment that turns raw experience into wisdom.
facts.libra1: The only zodiac sign represented by an object · once these scales were the claws of the neighboring scorpion.
facts.libra2: Saturn is exalted in Tula · the cosmic measure that weighs every action against its quiet counterweight.
facts.scorpio1: Antares, the scorpion's heart, is so vast it would swallow Mars' orbit if dropped where our Sun now stands.
facts.scorpio2: Vedic astrology calls this sign Vrishchika · tied to Ketu, the south lunar node and keeper of buried karmic threads.
facts.sagittarius1: Sagittarius points straight at the galactic core · the supermassive black hole Sgr A* lies inside its boundary.
facts.sagittarius2: Jupiter's fiery domain · in Vedic lore Dhanu is the archer of dharma, aiming the soul toward higher meaning.
facts.capricorn1: The sea-goat is one of the oldest mythic figures · drawn by the Sumerians more than four thousand years ago.
facts.capricorn2: Saturn rules here · Makara is the slow climb from the ocean's depths toward the disciplined summit of the world.
facts.aquarius1: The Aquarid meteor shower each May is debris from Halley's Comet · last seen in 1986 and not due back until 2061.
facts.aquarius2: Aquarius hosts the Helix Nebula, 650 light-years away · often called the Eye of God, gazing back from the dark.
facts.pisces1: Two fish swimming in opposite directions · the soul's final dissolve before rebirth into a fresh zodiac round.
facts.pisces2: Vedic astrology calls Pisces Meena · Jupiter's own sign and Venus's exaltation, the ocean where wisdom finally rests.
